name: Solid Defence vs 1.d4
summary: Against the queen-pawn opening, Black builds a solid pawn center, develops calmly, and answers each White setup with a matching plan.

goal.title: Build a solid center and develop behind it
goal.text: Black answers the queen-pawn opening by putting a pawn on the central square in front of the queen. Then the knights and bishops come out to safe squares behind it, Black castles, and waits for the right moment to hit White's center with a side pawn or a trade.
plans: Keep the center pawn defended by a knight and a pawn behind it.
Develop the king-side knight early, and bring the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before closing it in.
If White brings a bishop out early, copy it and trade it off.
Castle, then challenge White's center with a side pawn or by trading pieces.

variations.name: 2.c4: the Slav, take the pawn and keep the bishop out
variations.strategy: Material is level and Black's structure is healthy, with the c-pawn holding the center. Finish development and castle, then free the position with a central pawn break once the knights are placed. The light-squared bishop is outside the pawn chain, so keep it active and do not let a White pawn push harass it. The bishop pin on the knight is a lever: trade it when it helps, or keep it to tie White's pieces down.

variations.name: 2.Bf4: copy the bishop and trade it
variations.strategy: Black copies White's bishop and trades the dark-squared bishops, so the middlegame is calm with no weaknesses. Castle, bring the rooks to the center, and challenge White's center with a side pawn break once your knights are placed. After the trade White's rook has an open file toward your king side, so keep the pawns in front of your king intact and be ready for a pawn storm if White castles on the other wing.

variations.name: 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Bf4: develop, copy the bishop
variations.strategy: White gave a knight for your bishop, so White has two bishops and your pawns on the king side are doubled but safe. Keep the center closed with your pawns to blunt the bishops, develop the knights, and use the half-open file on the king side with a rook. Castling short is fine because the pawns still shield the king. Choose a moment for the c-pawn push to challenge the center.

variations.name: 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e3: the Colle setup
variations.strategy: White has built a compact setup aimed at pushing the central pawn forward. Black has castled in a classical position and should meet that push by trading pieces and using the open lines for the bishops. Pressure White's central pawn with the c-pawn, the knight and the queen. If White delays the push, play the e-pawn break yourself and open the position for your pieces.

variations.name: 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.g3: meet the fianchetto
variations.strategy: Black has a firm chain of pawns in the center. White's fianchettoed bishop eyes the center and the queen side, so keep it blocked by your central pawn. Finish the queen-side development, then either take on the center pawn to unblock your position and play the c-pawn push, or prepare the e-pawn break supported by both knights. White's bishop is slow, so do not rush.

variations.name: 2.e3 Nf6 3.Bd3: hit the center
variations.strategy: White is building a pawn wall with the f-pawn, which controls the key central square but also weakens the squares in front of it. Black fianchettoes the bishop, castles, and hits White's center with the c-pawn and a knight. Aim a knight at the weakened central square and trade White's active bishop when the chance comes. Keep your own pawn on the central square so White's bishop has little to hit.

variations.name: 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Bg5: stay solid
variations.strategy: Black has a very solid setup, but it is a little cramped, so the middlegame plan is to ease the space by trading pieces. Prepare the e-pawn break with the queen and a rook, and be ready for a central strike from White with the c-pawn or the e-pawn. Keep the knights coordinated, and do not let White's bishop pin the knight on the king side without a plan to unpin.
